name: What's the difference between a pergola and a gazebo?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between a pergola and a gazebo?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both pergolas and gazebos provide shade and define outdoor spaces, but they differ in structure and coverage. A pergola typically features an open, slatted roof supported by columns, offering partial shade and often acting as an architectural feature over a walkway or patio. It can be freestanding or attached to a house. A gazebo, conversely, is usually a freestanding, octagonal or circular structure with a solid, often pitched roof, providing full shade and shelter. Gazebos are more enclosed and often feature built-in seating.
acceptedAnswer.description: A pergola has an open, slatted roof offering partial shade, often over a patio. A gazebo is a freestanding structure with a solid, pitched roof providing full shade and shelter.
